limitations: One owner-confirmed SMS or MMS reference, one identity read and at most one conditional delete. The other transport holds a same-id row with the same thread and date, so a delete sent to the wrong table would remove it. The row's box can move into or out of a send (draft, outbox, queued or failed) at any time before the effect; only inbox and sent rows are settled. Two thread/date equality classes and two raw-date representations cover replacement and normalization races. Witness runs remove the authority recheck, the collection selection or the settled-box selection and must break their invariant. Owner confirmation and trustworthy platform affected-row counts are assumptions. Actual SQLite predicates and bridge guards are exercised by JVM cases; real Telephony permission/AppOp/role enforcement, Binder reliability, process death, carrier behavior and physical-device acceptance remain separate. Lost or invalid replies are unknown and grant no retry.
